name: infra_airflow_dag
title: Airflow DAG + a tasks package: four PythonOperator callables, and the leak in the ETL task
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-infra: the orchestrated project shape, where the pipeline is a DAG and not a script
note: One planted defect (MLV101 in the ETL task), recovered at 0.950. The project shape is the point: the DAG file contains no ML at all, every task body is reached only through a `python_callable=` reference, and the four task modules never call each other - they communicate through .npy and .json files on disk. MLView still reads all six files, finds the leak, and declares honest coverage gaps for airflow and pendulum. `--relevance ml` and `--relevance all` produce identical findings (6 files either way).
stagesObserved: config, data, preprocess, model, train, eval and deliver present; `objective` reported absent, which is correct for a gradient-boosting project with no explicit loss object.

expected.defect: the scaler is fitted on the whole feature matrix at line 49 and the train/holdout cut is made at line 51 from its output
expected.why: the mean and variance the model trains under were computed with every holdout row included, so the AUC the promote task gates on is optimistic and there is no way to recover the honest number after the fact

forbidden.why: this task fits no transformer of its own: the StandardScaler at line 27 is a step inside a Pipeline, so cross_val_score refits it per fold, and estimator.fit at line 45 is an estimator fit on x_train only
nothing is fitted in this file; the model is loaded from disk and only predict / predict_proba are called
no fit / fit_transform / partial_fit call exists in this file
the only fit here takes x_train, which the upstream task produced as the training partition
cross_val_score at line 41 is handed a Pipeline, not a bare estimator, so the scaler is refit inside every fold - which is exactly the fix this rule asks for
there is no temporal column here: `snapshot` is a partition key used to seed the synthetic draw, no date is parsed and nothing is sorted by time
f1_score and precision_recall_fscore_support are fed model.predict(...) - hard classes - which is what they take
roc_auc_score and average_precision_score are fed model.predict_proba(x_hold)[:, 1] at line 28, a score column, not hard labels
every splitter in the project passes random_state: train_test_split at prepare.py:52, StratifiedKFold at train.py:40, and the classifier at train.py:31
StratifiedKFold passes shuffle=True together with random_state=seed at line 40
this is joblib.dump of an sklearn Pipeline, not torch.save of a module, and nothing in the project calls torch.load

unsupported.defect: none - this is the correct spelling
unsupported.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2: MLV117 (`train_test_split` without `stratify` on a classification target) carries the status **later** in docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 1 and is not built, so a `forbidden` row for it is a label for a rule that cannot fire - which `analyzer/tests/accuracy/test_accuracy.py::test_every_labelled_code_is_a_real_rule` rejects, and it turned that shipped test red. The observation is kept here so the row can be restored verbatim the day MLV117 ships. Original note: train_test_split passes stratify=labels at line 52

LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2: MLV903 is not a built rule - it carries the status **later** in docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 1 - so a label for it can never be satisfied and can never be violated. `analyzer/tests/accuracy/test_accuracy.py::test_every_labelled_code_is_a_real_rule` rejects one, and this row turned that shipped test red. The observation is kept verbatim here so the row can be restored the day the rule ships. Original verdict `forbidden`, original note: every task callable is referenced from a PythonOperator in this DAG and the four are chained at line 65; none of them is an orphan
